headline: High-risk data and capability overlap: Copilot can read/write repo context while ComfyUI is offline-only, creating medium leakage/conflict and low prompt-injection risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, browser, or MCP bridge, so direct injection paths are limited. Copilot can read editor buffers and repo context, so if ComfyUI outputs are manually pasted into code files, Copilot could be steered by attacker-controlled text. This is a manual bridge, not a default channel.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are manually copied into files or editor buffers that Copilot reads
IF Copilot is used on content originating from ComfyUI prompts or generated metadata
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs out of code comments and prompt text
Review pasted content before opening it in Copilot-enabled buffers
Use separate workspaces for image-generation notes and source code
Disable Copilot on files that may contain untrusted generated text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot reads editor buffers and repo context by default, while ComfyUI touches models, workflows, seeds, and checkpoints. If those artifacts are placed in a shared workspace, Copilot can ingest them and transmit context to api.githubcopilot.com. ComfyUI is offline-only, so the leakage path is one-way through the shared workspace rather than from ComfyUI itself.
conditions: IF ComfyUI workflows, seeds, or checkpoints are stored in the same repo or editor buffers Copilot indexes
IF those artifacts contain secrets, proprietary prompts, or sensitive media metadata
mitigations: Move ComfyUI artifacts to a non-repo directory
Exclude workflow and seed files from Copilot-visible buffers
Strip secrets from prompts and metadata before saving
Use a separate Git repository for image-generation assets

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write filesystem changes and modify git state, while ComfyUI is an offline workflow system with asynchronous queueing and no multiple-instance support. If both operate on the same project tree, Copilot edits can race with ComfyUI-generated files or workflow assets. The profiles do not show locking, so conflict is plausible in default editor/repo use.
conditions: IF Copilot Workspace or editor edits the same directory that ComfyUI writes to
IF ComfyUI-generated assets are tracked in git and Copilot modifies them concurrently
mitigations: Keep generated assets outside the active git tree
Commit ComfyUI outputs in a dedicated branch
Avoid simultaneous edits to the same files
Use manual review before accepting Copilot edits

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can treat repository context as authoritative and propose edits, while ComfyUI can generate workflows and assets that may be copied into code or docs. If Copilot consumes ComfyUI-produced text without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code or workflow changes. The pair lacks an explicit verification gate in the profiles.
conditions: IF ComfyUI-generated instructions or metadata are pasted into Copilot-visible buffers
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits based on those unverified artifacts
mitigations: Require human review of all Copilot suggestions
Validate ComfyUI outputs before copying them into code
Keep generated prompts and code in separate files
Add a checklist for provenance before accepting edits

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not show PHI, EU-only residency, or special certifications. The main compliance issue is that Copilot sends context to a vendor API, while ComfyUI is offline-only; this creates a small policy mismatch only if regulated data is placed into Copilot-visible buffers. No stronger residency or certification conflict is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in files or buffers that Copilot can read
IF organizational policy forbids sending that data to vendor-hosted inference
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in Copilot-visible buffers
Use a local-only editor profile for sensitive work
Review retention and telemetry settings for Copilot
Separate regulated projects from image-generation assets
